## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vātaggasindhavajātaka* (Ja 266) is a narrative text preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection, with the verse incipit *Yenāsi kisiyā paṇḍu* [Fausböll 1879]. The frame story (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana near Sāvatthi, where the Buddha related the discourse regarding a certain landowner (*kuṭumbika*) and a beautiful woman who became infatuated with him [Fausböll 1879].

In the story of the past (*atītavatthu*), the Bodhisatta was reborn as Vātaggasindhava, the royal thoroughbred steed (*maṅgalassa*) of the king of Bārāṇasī, while the woman was identified with a she-ass (*gadrabhī*) [Fausböll 1879; Fausböll 1897]. At the conclusion of the teaching, after the proclamation of the Truths, the landowner was established in the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) [Fausböll 1879].
